summary: R-6 cab tower moved from Little Joe in 1977 now stands closed and unstaffed in Fish Creek State Park; the record's 9.1 m height matches the 1934 tower.

facts.design: R-6 flat cab on a 53-foot timber tower

access.note: Tower is closed to the public and fenced off; hikers can still reach the summit of Williams Peak.

visit.trail_note: About 3.4 miles round trip with over 1,200 feet of climbing; one writer rated it an easy hike.

corrections.why: 9.1 m is 30 feet, the height of the 1934 pole tower. The present tower is 53 feet tall, about 16.2 m.

corrections.proposed: 1969 built at Little Joe; 1977 relocated to Williams Peak
corrections.why: 1977 is the move to Williams Peak. Both sources date the erection at Little Joe to 1969.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register's Built field says 1977, but its own description and firelookout.com put the erection at Little Joe in 1969. Treated as built 1969 and relocated 1977.

The blog says the tower was hauled from Idaho in 1977. The register and firelookout.com describe the 1977 move from Little Joe, with the Idaho exhibit earlier. Both can be true, so the story reports the Little Joe stop.

sources.title: Mount Williams Lookout in Fish Creek State Park

notes_for_editor: Build year disputed: the register's Built field says 1977, while the erection at Little Joe is dated 1969. Height 53 ft converted to 16.2 m. Staffing as_of is the blog date; the firelookout list of personnel is undated beyond 1953-1959. No rental information found in the sources read. Did not use the AllTrails, PNWSOTA or Facebook search snippets as sources.
